packages.label: תַּלְמוּד וְלִילִית
packages.reason: The sole bechina in Torah #214 is a gematria identity: תַּלְמוּד = לִילִית = 480. The Rebbe explicitly grounds this as a structural equivalence: 'תַּלְמוּד בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁל שְׁמָהּ לִילִית'. This is the classic Rebbe Nachman gematria-bechina: identical numerical value reveals deep structural kinship — the same underlying reality expressed through two names. The package is marked neutral because this bechina is the Torah's entire point: the Talmud and Lilith share the same structural nature (the letters of one are the gematria of the other), and this shared nature is precisely what makes Talmud study a double-edged spiritual force. Properly oriented learning (כַּהֹגֶן) subdues Lilith by the power of this identity — it turns her own gematria-signature back against her. Improperly oriented learning empowers her through the same mechanism. The package therefore does not belong to the good domain alone (תַּלְמוּד as pure Torah study) nor to the evil domain alone (לִילִית as pure adversary), but occupies the structural boundary between both poles. This is not a contradiction but a deep structural feature: the same neutral vessel can be filled with holiness or with evil depending on orientation, and its power in either direction derives from the same shared nature.

stats.note_on_structure: Torah #214 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — 2 sentences, recorded as a condensed oral transmission (the text ends with a colon, indicating a truncated record). Its single bechina is the gematria equivalence תַּלְמוּד = לִילִית = 480. The eitza chain (which is the practical application) is: לִמּוּד כַּהֹגֶן → הַכְנָעַת לִילִית / לִמּוּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי → כֹּחַ לִילִית. The eitza flows between the bechina-identity (Package 1) and the outcomes, but the outcomes themselves are not bechina nodes — they describe the directional consequences of the Talmud/Lilith structural identity depending on how it is oriented. The three additional concepts (בַּעַל דָּבָר, לִמּוּד כַּהֹגֶן, לִמּוּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי) appear in the source text but only through eitza language and do not form bechina packages.
